name: Clinical Pathology Foundation Models Benchmark
description: The use of self-supervised learning (SSL) to train pathology foundation models has increased substantially in the past few years. Notably, several models trained on large quantities of clinical data have been made publicly available in recent months. This will significantly enhance scientific research in computational pathology and help bridge the gap between research and clinical deployment. With the increase in availability of public foundation models of different sizes, trained using different algorithms on different datasets, it becomes important to establish a benchmark to compare the performance of such models on a variety of clinically relevant tasks spanning multiple organs and diseases. In this work, we present a collection of pathology datasets comprising clinical slides associated with clinically relevant endpoints including cancer diagnoses and a variety of biomarkers generated during standard hospital operation from two medical centers. We leverage these datasets to systematically assess the performance of public pathology foundation models and provide insights into best practices for training new foundation models and selecting appropriate pretrained models.
evaluation_method: AUROC (primary) and accuracy / F1 for classification tasks
typical_sota_score: varies by task and biomarker; commonly reported AUROC ranges ~0.70–0.95 across different endpoints
reputation: An emerging, task-diverse benchmark for pathology foundation models with growing interest in the computational pathology community.
notes: Medical imaging benchmark: non-LLM, uses clinical slide data with potential site-specific biases; risk of pretraining/data contamination across models; requires domain expertise for interpretation and has regulatory/privacy considerations.
